karate-core: Suite.cancel(reason), the IDE event profile and RUN_COMPLETE. cancel is idempotent and distinct from abort: every live scenario's HTTP client is cancelled (a registry of runtimes, registered before karate-config.js evaluates; the client aborts the call in flight and refuses every later one, so a script that catches the aborted request cannot send another), the step loop, call loops, callonce and config calls stop at the next boundary, a retry-until poll wakes from its sleep (a latch, not Thread.sleep), and a dynamic outline whose setup is cancelled records the outline's own result, if selected, and the enumeration goes on. HttpClient.cancel() is sticky where abort() is one-shot, and its javadoc binds a wrapping client to delegate it. An unfinished scenario reads cancelled — StepResult.Status.CANCELLED for the step in flight whether it threw or returned after the cancel, ScenarioResult.isCancelled as the whole verdict (not failed, no @fail inversion), never passed — and so does every scenario and feature not yet started, an abortSuiteOnFailure already in force notwithstanding: the run enumerates what it would have selected (SCENARIO_ENTER and EXIT fired back to back, no config, no step), the same count Suite.getScenarioTotal pre-computes from FeatureRuntime.countSelected, so a cancelled run's total equals passed + failed + cancelled, each scenario counted once; FeatureResult and SuiteResult.isPassed are false. The outcome reaches results, JSONL, HTML (badge, scenario_cancelled, status), JUnit (a skipped testcase the testsuite counts) and Cucumber. Runner.Builder.ideEvents dispatches every event under one lock stamped with a run-wide gap-free sequence (RunEvent.getSequence), an event fired from inside a listener queued until the current one has reached every listener (a listener that throws strands nothing: the queue drains, the first failure is rethrown after), and streams STEP_LOG chunks before STEP_EXIT, hook output carrying no step; JsonLinesEventWriter.envelope carries runId (Runner.Builder.runId), executionIndex — allocated before config evaluates, so config-time output and calls resolve — and the calling scenario and step; outline rows carry exampleTableIndex; PROGRESS fires per top-level scenario, counted under the lock. RUN_CANCEL fires from cancel and never after RUN_COMPLETE, which waits for a publishing cancel (an interrupt is restored after the barrier, not a way past it) and after which cancel returns false; RUN_COMPLETE follows driver and mock teardown, ext shutdown and every report write, and is the JSONL's last line. KaratePom names xplorer reserved; OutputPom.dir defaults to null so run and clean fall through to the build tool's dir, and a bare karate prints help when the pom names no paths. Tests: SuiteCancelTest (16: a call loop of 2000 rows, retry until at a 5 s interval, parallel(4), karate-config.js, callonce in Background and with three parallel waiters confirmed blocked on its lock, an HTTP call to a stub that never answers, three features with a dynamic outline cancelled while the first runs, two calls in one step, a final step returning after the cancel, a dynamic outline's setup, abort then cancel serial and parallel, @fail, a cancel after completion, an @ignore dynamic outline cancelled in setup, an interrupted completion barrier — each within 325 ms of cancel with the call aborted and the pre-run total accounted for), IdeEventProfileTest (3: ids, sequence across threads, STEP_LOG before STEP_EXIT, two Examples tables, PROGRESS, RUN_COMPLETE after report, driver and mock teardown; config-time ids, a re-entrant cancelling listener, teardown output; a listener that cancels and throws), PomLayoutTest (gradle and maven, in a CLI subprocess). 10x repeat green. karate-core -Pcicd 3221/0/0 (4 skipped), karate-js 1884/0/0 (2 skipped).
